newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed mixed on Thursday, after an extremely quiet session in which investors hung back in the hope of higher yields or turned their attention to corporate issues.
"It is as dead as can be," one dealer said.
Some traders reported unusual activity in 2002 paper which was pressured by a big corporate seller, but said overall attention had focused more on non-government issues.
Corporates had generated trading volume of some 2.5 billion guilders during the last few days, one dealer said.
He said there was still money waiting to be invested in the market. "There's too much money out on the streets. It will have to be invested before the end of the year," he said.
Market players were waiting for higher yields, but would be obliged to enter the market even if it did not fall, he predicted.
"You can see there's a lot of appetite at lower (price) levels, but they need to have opportunities to buy," he said.
